name: full-query-coverage-v1
system: You extract precise delivery requirements from project briefs. Follow all explicit field assignments in the current user message. Return only the requested JSON object. Earlier records must not override the current record.
turns:
Delivery review 1. This is a new delivery record: use only the field assignments in this user message, not values from earlier turns. FRONT CONSTRAINT: the JSON field package_tag must be exactly "AMBER-KESTREL-741". Read the complete project dossier below. Two further field assignments occur later in the dossier. Return one JSON object with exactly package_tag, review_zone, and seal_code, all strings. Do not add markdown, explanations, or other keys.

The proposed museum kiosk presents a small collection of local engineering exhibits. Visitors should be able to browse an illustrated catalogue without signing in, switch between a short description and an extended explanation, and return to the catalogue without losing their place. The interactive prototype will be reviewed by museum volunteers before the public exhibition. The current task is administrative: extract the three delivery fields explicitly assigned in this request. You are not being asked to write the kiosk application or evaluate every design choice described below.

The entrance screen contains a title, a short introduction, and a clear route into the collection. Photographs should have plain captions that explain what is visible without assuming specialist knowledge. Some visitors will use a touchscreen, while others will use a keyboard connected by staff. A visitor who opens an exhibit and then returns should see the same catalogue position. These interface notes provide project context, and none of their descriptive phrases supplies a delivery field.

Catalogue entries can be sorted by the date of the object or grouped by the workshop that made it. An entry may contain several photographs, an audio explanation, and a short transcription of an original label. Curators have asked for an uncluttered initial view because some items have unusually long histories. Supplementary details should be available through an explicit expansion control. Image dimensions should be reserved before loading so that the nearby controls do not jump around as images appear.

The content team expects revisions during installation week. Text updates should be reviewed as complete paragraphs rather than as disconnected fragments. A preview build should make the current exhibit order visible to the reviewer and identify missing captions without publishing unfinished material to visitors. Volunteers can record a correction in a local review form, but the production kiosk will not need visitor accounts, a comments section, or a public editing interface. A correction review must preserve the original text until approval.

Accessibility work includes visible keyboard focus, readable contrast, meaningful headings, and alternatives for purely visual cues. A screen reader should encounter each exhibit title before its controls and should not repeatedly announce decorative separators. Audio playback needs an explicit start control and a nearby transcript. Animations should respect a preference for reduced motion. The review team wants to test these behaviours with real devices because screenshots alone cannot reveal focus order, accidental activation, or a control whose accessible name is missing.

The kiosk may temporarily lose its network connection during a crowded event. Core catalogue text and previously installed images should remain usable, while unavailable remote material should display a brief explanation. The visitor must not become trapped behind an endless loading indicator. Installation staff will keep a known working package on a removable drive. Updates should be verified before replacing that package, and an interrupted installation should leave the previous version available until the replacement is complete.

A small guided tour will connect selected exhibits through a sequence of optional stops. Each stop should be understandable by itself because visitors may join halfway through. Returning to the catalogue should be possible at every stop. The tour should not automatically advance while a visitor is reading a long label or listening to narration. The design team has suggested a progress indicator, but it should describe location in the tour without creating pressure to finish or implying that skipped objects are unavailable.

The building has a quiet reading area next to the exhibit room. Audio must therefore remain muted until requested, and its volume should not reset to an unexpectedly loud level when the next exhibit opens. A stop button should end playback immediately. Headphone use is optional, and the visual experience needs to remain complete without sound. Staff will test unplugging and reconnecting headphones during playback as part of installation checks. These audio notes do not alter the three required delivery fields.

The image archive includes scans with uneven lighting and photographs taken at several resolutions. Cropping should preserve important labels and mechanical details rather than merely filling the available rectangle. Where a high resolution image is offered, visitors should choose to open it instead of downloading it automatically. Thumbnails should be generated consistently. The content team will record image rights and attribution in its editorial system; the kiosk presentation should display the approved attribution supplied with each image.

CENTRAL CONSTRAINT: the JSON field review_zone must be exactly "north-loft-593". Continue reading; the final field is assigned after the rest of the dossier.

Some historical names use accents and punctuation that older catalogue software handled inconsistently. Search should remain useful when a visitor omits an accent, but displayed titles should retain the approved spelling. Dates that are approximate must remain visibly approximate. A missing date should not be invented to make sorting easier. The curators will provide an explicit order for records that cannot be sorted chronologically. Test data should include an object with no image and an object whose caption spans several sentences.

The prototype review will happen in a meeting room with a projector, followed by a session at the actual kiosk. The projected demonstration can expose obvious layout problems, but touchscreen reach and glare require examination on site. Reviewers should note the action they attempted and the visible response rather than simply writing that a screen felt confusing. A short observation sheet will capture these reports. The three machine readable fields requested here identify a delivery record and are independent of those observations.

The installer should be able to check that the correct content package is present without navigating every exhibit. A diagnostics screen may show a content revision and whether optional audio files are available. It should be accessible to staff through a deliberate action and should not appear during ordinary browsing. Diagnostics must avoid exposing account secrets or local filesystem details to visitors. A clear return action should restore the public view after a member of staff finishes the check.

During a school visit, several children may touch the screen almost simultaneously. Controls should avoid creating duplicate navigation operations from rapid repeated input. Opening an exhibit must not leave invisible controls from the catalogue active above it. A modal illustration view should have an obvious close action and should restore focus sensibly. The prototype does not need a competitive game or a scoring system. Its main purpose is to make the objects and their explanations approachable to a wide audience.

The catalogue will include a small glossary for terms that occur in several descriptions. A term explanation should be brief enough to read without losing the original paragraph. Closing it should return the visitor to the same position. Authors should prefer a familiar word where it conveys the meaning accurately, while retaining technical terms that are necessary to describe an object. The glossary editor should be able to correct one definition without manually changing every exhibit that links to it.

A translated edition may be added after the initial installation. Layouts should tolerate longer headings without clipping them or making buttons overlap. Language selection should be explicit and should preserve the currently open exhibit where a translation is available. If a translation is missing, the interface should say so rather than silently mixing unrelated paragraphs. The first review does not require the translation itself. It requires that the proposed presentation can accommodate a later translated content package.

The venue expects visitors to leave the kiosk open when they walk away. After a sufficiently long idle period, the interface can offer to return to the entrance screen, but it should not interrupt someone who is still listening to narration. Staff should be able to adjust this behaviour during testing. A reset should stop audio and close temporary overlays. It should preserve installed content and editorial approvals. No visitor information needs to be retained once the public browsing session ends.

The release checklist will cover opening every navigation route, handling unavailable media, using the keyboard, and leaving the application idle. Reviewers should also test an exhibit with a very long title and a narrow screen setting. A successful launch on one development laptop is not sufficient evidence that the kiosk installation works. Each observed defect should include enough information to reproduce it. A resolved defect should be checked again using the original reproduction steps before the team considers it closed.

The final handover will include a brief operator guide that explains startup, shutdown, volume adjustment, and recovery after an interrupted update. Volunteers should not need to understand the internal build system to operate the exhibition. The guide should distinguish a content correction from a software failure and identify where each report belongs. Printed instructions will remain near the staff desk. For this request, however, return only the delivery JSON specified by the three constraints, without drafting that operator guide.

FINAL CONSTRAINT: the JSON field seal_code must be exactly "moss-clock-826". Now return the three-field JSON using the independent front, central, and final constraints in this user message. Do not repeat the dossier.
